speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for your response. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision with black spots in the right eye, I need to know if these visual changes started suddenly or gradually.

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy  
REQUEST TEST: Ocular_Coagulation_Profile

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. Normal readings for Ocular_Coagulation_Profile.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very helpful clue; however, I must clarify that while TB can affect the eye, your specific symptoms of black spots and decreased vision in an AIDS patient are highly characteristic of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. To confirm this, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a "curtain" coming over your vision?

REQUEST TEST: CMV_DNA_PCR
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Photo_Right_Eye

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CMV_DNA_PCR: Positive for Cytomegalovirus. Fundus_Photo_Right_Eye: Shows extensive retinal necrosis with yellow-white granular opacities and hemorrhages consistent with CMV retinitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis. The positive CMV PCR and fundus photos showing retinal necrosis with yellow-white granular opacities confirm this diagnosis in your immunocompromised state. Given the extensive involvement, we need to start antiviral therapy immediately to prevent further vision loss. Do you have any history of renal disease or other drug allergies that might affect our treatment plan?
